findings.claim: Live delivery can continue issuing checkpoints after subscription authority is revoked for out-of-scope or object-denied events because the subscribe relation is only rechecked for object-authorized matching mutations.
findings.evidence: Acceptance task 2 requires per-event authority and task 4 requires revocation to meet the contract; in `delivery_frame`, the checkpoint is issued before filtering, tenant/type mismatches return `Ok(EntityTypeWatchFrame::CheckpointAdvanced(checkpoint))` without checking `producer.subscribe_tuple`, object-denied events also return `CheckpointAdvanced`, and the subscribe recheck appears only inside the `Ok(true)` object-view branch before returning `Mutation`.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the subscribe tuple after any delivery is read and before issuing or returning any checkpoint/mutation frame, treating false/error as `Terminal::Permission`, not only in the object-authorized mutation branch.
